steps.issue: Leading / trailing spaces in text fields
steps.action: Trimmed whitespace on all 19 text columns.
steps.why: ' Cardiology ' and 'Cardiology' would otherwise be counted as two departments.

steps.action: Mapped 22 raw labels to 10 canonical department names (case-insensitive lookup table).
steps.why: Variants such as 'SURGERY / OR', 'laboratory' and ' Pharmacy ' split one department into several groups.

steps.action: Checked full-row duplicates and repeated visit_id values; none found, no rows removed.
steps.why: Duplicate visits would inflate volumes and costs.

steps.action: Parsed visit_date to a real date type (ISO format); confirmed the four 0/1 flag columns are integers.
steps.why: Needed for time-series charts, date slicers and rate calculations.

steps.action: Recalculated as department_cost_burden / (resource_utilization_index / 100) and flagged in cost_imputed.
steps.why: The identity burden = cost x utilization / 100 holds in every complete row (max relative error 0.0860%), so the value is recovered rather than guessed.

steps.action: Filled with the median score of the same department and flagged in satisfaction_imputed.
steps.why: Only 1.1% of rows; the median is robust to the skewed 1-5 scale and keeps the visit in every other KPI.

steps.issue: Possible inconsistent derived fields and out-of-range values
steps.action: Ran 10 rule checks (calendar fields vs visit_date, age_group vs age, value ranges, flag logic). All passed; no corrections needed.
steps.why: Confirms the pre-computed calendar and grouping columns can be trusted in the model.

steps.issue: Fields needed for analysis were not in the extract
steps.action: Added care_setting, month_start, month_name, month_num, wait_over_target, occupancy_over_target, high_strain and bottleneck_count.
steps.why: Supports drill-up by care setting, monthly trends, target-breach rates and bottleneck analysis.

steps.issue: bottleneck_reason holds several values in one cell (separated by ';')
steps.action: Split into a bridge table with one row per visit and reason (1549 rows).
steps.why: A multi-valued text cell cannot be counted or filtered; the bridge keeps the fact table at one row per visit.

known_limitations: The extract is a simulated / anonymised dataset: every patient_id appears once, so repeat-visit analysis is not possible.
er_wait_time_minutes is recorded for every department, not only the ED; the dashboard labels it 'wait time'.
Some values sit on fixed limits (wait time floor 2.0 min, occupancy cap 99%, length of stay floor 0.03 days), which suggests the source system clips extremes.
No-show visits still carry cost and length-of-stay values in the source; they are kept as supplied.
All six target_* columns hold one constant value each, so targets are hospital-wide, not per department.
